gloss: one or more: no plural ending
title: Plurals: buku-buku and banyak
pattern: buku (book, books) · dua buku · banyak orang · buku-buku
explanation: Indonesian nouns don't change for more than one: buku is 'book' or 'books', and the situation tells you which. A number or banyak (lots of, many) goes before the noun, which stays as it is: dua buku (two books), banyak orang (lots of people). Saying a noun twice, buku-buku, also makes it plural, with a feel of many different ones; it's commoner in writing than in conversation.
natural: Leave nouns single almost all the time: Ada banyak turis di sini (There are lots of tourists here). A few doubled words are everyday speech, though: anak-anak (the kids) and teman-teman (friends, everyone).
stiff: Don't double a noun after a number or banyak: dua anak-anak and banyak orang-orang are wrong, because the number has already said 'more than one'. And there's no need to mark the plural where English must: Saya suka buku is 'I like books'.

examples.english: I'd like to buy two tickets.

gap.why: After a number the noun stays single: dua tiket.

examples.english: There are lots of people here.

gap.why: Banyak has already said 'many', so orang stays single.
Sepatu is one shoe or a pair: no need to double it.

examples.english: The kids are playing on the beach.

gap.why: Anak-anak is the everyday 'the kids'; after banyak it would stay single, banyak anak.
